extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing applications for the NIH Director’s Pioneer Award (DP1)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a single-PI application to the NIH Director’s Pioneer Award (DP1), including required Essay content, letters of reference, eligibility/registration, and meeting the program's novelty and effort-commitment expectations. Focus is on articulating highly innovative, high-impact, and substantially different research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and primary expectations of the Pioneer Award program
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports individual scientists of exceptional creativity who propose highly innovative research projects with the potential to produce a major impact on broad, important areas relevant to the mission of NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should reflect the full diversity of the nation’s research workforce. Applications in all topics relevant to NIH’s mission are welcome (behavioral, social, biomedical, applied, formal sciences; basic, translational, or clinical research). To be considered pioneering, proposed research must reflect substantially different scientific directions from those already being pursued in the investigator’s research program or elsewhere; it must not be an obvious extension or scale-up of current research. The program emphasizes qualities of the investigator, innovativeness, and potential impact. Preliminary data and detailed experimental plans are not requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — applicant and organization types
rubrics_metrics.description: Which individuals and organizations may apply and which may not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible organizations include a wide range of domestic entities (institutions of higher education, nonprofits, for-profits, governments, tribal entities, etc.). Non-domestic (non-U.S.) entities are not eligible to apply; non-domestic components of U.S. organizations are not eligible. Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary may be PD/PI. Only single PD/PI applications are allowed; multiple PD(s)/PI(s) will not be accepted. Individuals may serve as the PD/PI on only one application for this FOA. Applicant organizations may submit more than one scientifically distinct application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registrations and identifiers before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations that applicant organizations and PD(s)/PI(s) must complete prior to application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must obtain and maintain DUNS, SAM registration (including CAGE/NCAGE as applicable), eRA Commons registration (PD/PI must have an eRA Commons account), and Grants.gov registration. Registrations can take many weeks; complete them well in advance. The same DUNS must be used across registrations. Failure to complete registrations is not an allowable reason for late submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PD/PI and limitations on key personnel materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the PD/PI may serve as senior/key personnel and submit a biographical sketch; collaborators/collaborator biosketches and letters of collaboration are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan. Research and Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) - Additional Biographical Sketch(es): DO NOT USE. Letters of collaboration will not be accepted. Information on collaborators may be included in the Essay and their names and affiliations should be listed in the PHS Assignment Request Form. For assignment requests, list collaborators' names and affiliations and any individuals you request not to review (with rationale); NIH will consider but is not bound to accept such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort commitment requirement for awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: Required minimum research effort the PD/PI must commit to the Pioneer Award project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pioneer awardees must commit the major portion (more than 6 person-months or at least 51%) to activities supported by the Pioneer Award in the first three years. Effort may be reduced to a minimum of 4 person-months (33%) in year four and 3 person-months (25%) in year five. Effort toward teaching, administrative, or clinical duties should not be included. Applicants with current research commitments equal to 6 person-months or more must adjust existing grant effort to meet these minima. Investigators unable to meet this requirement should not apply. An explicit statement of research effort commitment must be included in the Essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirement and referee guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Three (and only three) confidential letters of reference are required and must be submitted by referees via eRA Commons by the application due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications missing letters of reference will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed. Letters must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. (local time of the referee) on the application due date; late letters are not accepted. Instructions for referees: In two pages or less, describe the applicant’s qualities that support the claim to scientific innovativeness and creativity; give specific examples when possible; address the likelihood that the applicant will conduct groundbreaking research. Letters must include the applicant’s name at top and a signature block (full name, title, institution, contact info). Referees do not need an eRA Commons account; they must use the specified link and provide the applicant's eRA Commons User ID. Previously submitted letters from prior years will not be retrieved; referees must submit new letters for this cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy Essay — required sections and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Strategy is supplied as a single Essay.pdf and must contain specific sections in the given order with exact headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essay must begin with the two 1-digit scientific area codes and abbreviations (primary; secondary). Required sections and headings (in order): Scientific Areas (codes), Project Title, Project description, Evidence of PD's/PI's innovativeness, How the planned research differs from the PD's/PI's past or current work, Suitability for Pioneer Award program, Statement of research effort commitment. The essay should describe the innovative vision for addressing a major challenge or opportunity, why it's important, and the applicant's qualifications. No detailed experimental plan should be provided; the plan is expected to evolve. References are not required but may be included in the Essay and count toward the page limit. Figures/illustrations may be included but must fit within the page limit. Name the PDF 'Essay.pdf' and attach in the Research Strategy slot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on specific application components (Specific Aims, Bibliography, Appendix, certain forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain standard SF424/R&R components are disallowed or restricted for this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims: Do not use. Bibliography & References Cited: DO NOT USE (essential refs may be included in the essay within the page limit). Equipment, Other Attachments, Other biosketches, Multiple PD/PI plan, Letters of Support: DO NOT USE. A detailed budget and other budget forms are not requested and will not be accepted; only the five-year direct cost total should be entered. Appendix materials are limited; follow SF424 (R&R) Application Guide for allowed Appendix content. Progress Report Publication List: Do not use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and project period limits and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary limits, project duration, and how to report totals on forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards: $700,000 in direct costs per year plus applicable F&A. Project period limited to five years. On SF424 Cover: enter start date 09/30/2022 and end date 07/31/2027; enter total federal funds requested $3,500,000 (five-year direct cost total). Do not include F&A in the budget request. A detailed budget form is not requested and will not be accepted; request funds for personnel (including collaborators), supplies, equipment, subcontracts, and allowable costs within the five-year direct cost total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and detailed experimental plans not required (and not expected)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FOA explicitly states preliminary data and detailed experimental plans are not requested and applications should not present detailed experimental plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are recommended to prominently indicate that neither a detailed experimental plan nor extensive preliminary data are being provided per the FOA. However, reviewers must still have a clear sense of the overall research and be convinced the research will be pursued in a robust and rigorous manner. Since preliminary data are not required or expected, post-submission policies' Special Exception does NOT apply for adding preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in research direction as a programmatic requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed project must represent a new and distinct direction for the applicant and not be a logical extension or scale-up of existing efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in research direction is considered one that is not a logical extension or scale-up of ongoing efforts, but motivated by a fundamental new insight prompting a new line of research or substantial departure. While the new direction may rest on prior expertise, it cannot be an obvious extension suitable for a conventional NIH mechanism (e.g., R01). Applications that are straightforward extensions of ongoing research should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion — Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assign an overall impact score reflecting likelihood the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) in consideration of review criteria and additional review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact is informed by the scored review criteria (below) and additional considerations. Applications do not need to be strong in all individual categories to be judged likely to have major impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or critical barrier? How will outcomes improve knowledge, capability, or clinical practice and change concepts/methods/technologies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials: assess whether the rationale and need for the trial are well supported by preliminary/preclinical data or literature; for trials with clinical/public health endpoints, is the trial necessary for testing safety/efficacy that could change practice or policy? For mechanistic/physiologic endpoints, is the trial needed to advance understanding?

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion — Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the PD/PI well suited to the project? Evidence for past innovation and ability to commit sufficient effort are considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the PD/PI’s qualifications, experience, training, and past record of innovation. Early Stage Investigators and those early in independent careers are considered for appropriate experience/training. Evidence of innovativeness (examples of integration across disciplines, questioning paradigms, persistence, ability to work across disciplines, energy and concentration) should be provided in the Essay and may be addressed in referees' letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion — Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the project uses novel concepts, approaches, or methods that challenge existing paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation here is tied to being pioneering: proposals may pose radically unconventional hypotheses or exceptionally innovative approaches. For Pioneer, innovativeness and fundamental novelty of the research direction are essential review elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion — Approach (adapted for Pioneer format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although detailed experimental plans are not required, reviewers will assess whether the research can be pursued in a robust and rigorous manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Essay should give reviewers a clear sense of the overall research to be pursued and convince them of rigor and feasibility at a high level. The writing should target broadly knowledgeable scientists across domains. For clinical trials, design and methods must be appropriate and conformance to administering IC policies is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration — Human subjects, clinical trials, and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, human subjects, clinical research, and NIH-defined clinical trials must follow SF424 Application Guide instructions and will be evaluated on human subjects protections and inclusion across ages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one human subjects study record if human subjects are involved. Clinical trials must follow IC clinical trial research policies; NIH expects registration and results reporting on ClinicalTrials.gov. Reviewers will assess rationale and need for trials, protections, and inclusion of individuals of all ages; refer to Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration — Vertebrate animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee will evaluate proposed use of live vertebrate animals using specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess (1) description of procedures including species/strains/ages/sex/total numbers; (2) justification for animals vs alternatives and species appropriateness; (3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain, injury; (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA guidelines. See Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration — Biohazards and select agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of potential hazards to personnel/environment and plans for biosafety, biocontainment, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether materials/procedures are hazardous and whether adequate protection is proposed. For Select Agent research, provide the select agent(s), registration status of entities, monitoring procedures for possession/use/transfer, and plans for biosafety/biocontainment/security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration — Resource sharing and authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource sharing plans and authentication of key biological/chemical resources will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource sharing plans are expected as Just-in-Time information if an award is considered. For key biological/chemical resources, reviewers will comment on brief plans for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources (authentication of cell lines, reagents, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period of support review consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although no detailed budget is submitted, reviewers will judge whether the requested funds and five-year period are justified relative to the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application compliance, completeness, and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be evaluated for completeness, conformance to SF424 (R&R) Application Guide, and responsiveness to FOA-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliant, incomplete, or nonresponsive applications may be delayed or not accepted for review. All page limitations described in the Application Guide and Table of Page Limits must be followed. Applicants should apply early to allow time for submission corrections. Paper applications are not accepted. Use ASSIST, Grants.gov Workspace, or institutional system-to-system solutions as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: What post-submission materials are acceptable and when they are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only documents informing of unforeseen events (e.g., natural disasters) that substantially affect the ability to execute the proposed research will be accepted as post-submission materials. The Special Exception to the post-submission policy for preliminary data does NOT apply to these applications (preliminary data are not expected).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and second-level decision considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria beyond peer-review scores that NIH/Council of Councils will use in funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding decisions consider: scientific/technical merit from peer review, availability of funds, relevance to program priorities including potential for investigator to lead groundbreaking research despite risks, unusually cross-cutting science, scientific balance in the Pioneer portfolio, potential to invigorate exceptionally innovative science nationally, and conformance to administering IC clinical trial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview stage for top candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-ranked applicants will be invited to an interview stage as part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates identified as most outstanding will be invited for interviews (April 2022) conducted virtually or in person. Interviews are conducted by a panel of outside experts and use the same review criteria as the written review.
